Introduction
This course
"Fundamentals of Agronomy – ASAG 1101" lays the foundation for the
study of crop production and field-crop management. It introduces the
definition, meaning and scope of Agronomy, its relationship with other
disciplines of Agricultural Science, and the classification and importance of
field crops. Students learn the principles of seeds and sowing, factors
governing crop-stand establishment, and the tillage operations and crop
geometry that shape a healthy crop stand. A substantial part of the course
builds understanding of crop nutrition — essential nutrients, their absorption
and the sources, classification and management of manures, fertilizers and
bio-fertilizers, including Integrated Nutrient Management and green manuring.
The course further develops knowledge of water resources and soil moisture
constants, and introduces the basics of weeds and their control. It concludes
with the agroclimatic zones and cropping systems of India, the principles of
sustainable crop production, allelopathy, and the factors governing crop growth
and development. Practical sessions provide hands-on exposure to the
instructional farm, identification of crops, seeds, fertilizers and weeds,
operation of tillage and inter-cultivation implements, and numerical exercises
on seed rate, plant population, fertilizer requirement and yield estimation.
Course Objective
The primary objectives of this
course are to:
●
To impart the basic and fundamental knowledge of
Agronomy.
●
To understand various agronomic terms.
●
To have hands-on experience of the basic agronomic
practices.

Course Content
Theory (Credit: 2)
Module I: Introduction to
Agronomy, Seeds and Crop Establishment
●
Definition, meaning and scope of Agronomy; art, science
and business of crop production
●
Relation of Agronomy with other disciplines of
Agricultural Science
●
Field crops and their classification, importance,
ecology and ecosystem
●
Seeds and sowing: definitions of crop, variety and seed
●
Factors affecting crop stand establishment: good
quality seed, proper tillage, time of sowing, seed rate
●
Depth and method of sowing: broadcasting, drilling,
dibbling, transplanting etc.
Module II: Tillage, Crop
Geometry and Crop Growth
●
Tillage and tilth: definition, objectives, types,
advantages and disadvantages
●
Conservation tillage
●
Crop density and geometry: plant geometry and planting
geometry
●
Effect of crop geometry on growth and yield
●
Growth and development of crops: definition, meaning
and factors affecting growth and development
Module III: Crop Nutrition,
Manures and Fertilizers
●
Essential nutrients: definition, criteria of
essentiality, functional elements
●
Classification of essential nutrients; role of macro
and micro nutrients
●
Nutrient absorption: active and passive absorption of
nutrients; forms of plant nutrients absorbed (combined/uncombined forms)
●
Manures and fertilizers: sources of nutrients —
inorganic (fertilizers), organic (manures) and bio-fertilizers; their
classification and characteristics
●
Integrated Nutrient Management (INM): meaning,
different approaches and advantages
●
Green manure: definition, objectives, types, desirable
characteristics, advantages and limitations of green manuring
Module IV: Water Management
and Weeds
●
Water resources of the world, India and the state
●
Soil moisture constants: gravitational water, capillary
water, hygroscopic water
●
Weeds: definition, importance and basics of
classification of weeds
●
Basics of weed control
Module V: Cropping Systems,
Sustainable Agriculture and Numerical Exercises
●
Agroclimatic zones of India and the state
●
Cropping systems: factors affecting cropping systems
●
Major cropping patterns and systems in the country
●
Sustainable crop production: definition, importance and
practices; natural resources and conservation; pollution and pollutants
●
Allelopathy: meaning and importance in crop production
●
Numerical exercises in agronomy: calculation of seed,
plant population, fertilizer requirement, herbicide requirement, water
requirement and yield estimation

Guidelines for Presentation
●
Structure the presentation with a clear introduction,
body, and conclusion, ensuring logical flow.
●
All students have to be presented on the day of
presentation.
●
The time allotted will be a maximum of 10 minutes for
each student. Failure to adhere to the time limit will result in reduction of
marks.
●
Presentation will be followed by a Q&A session.
●
Plagiarism is not allowed.
Guidelines for Writing Assignments
Assignments must be presented in
the following format:
●
Assignments must be own hand written.
●
All pages must be numbered.
●
The assignment must have a front cover containing the
course title, course code, the title of the assignment, name and registration
number of the student submitting the work, and submission date.
General Course Policy
●
The students are expected to be punctual for the class.
●
The students must follow the guidelines given for
presentations.
●
Assignments have to be submitted on time.
●
Plagiarism or cheating will not be tolerated regardless
of any other performance considerations. Students are not allowed to compromise
the integrity of the academic process at any cost; breaching the same will
subject them to disciplinary action.
●
Students are encouraged to clarify their doubts in the
classroom and outside, if any.
Sample Study Material
1. Scope of Agronomy (
CO1)
Agronomy is the branch of
agricultural science dealing with the theory and practice of field-crop
production and soil management.
AspectDescription
ArtSkill
of a farmer developed through experience in growing crops
ScienceSystematic
body of knowledge based on principles governing crop growth
BusinessEconomic
dimension of crop production for profit and livelihood
ScopeCovers
crop production, soil management, water management, weed management and
cropping systems
2. Classification of Tillage (
CO3)
Tillage operations are broadly
classified based on the stage and purpose of soil manipulation.
TypeDescriptionExample
Primary
Tillage		Deep
tillage carried out after harvest to break compact soil		Ploughing
with mould board plough
Secondary
Tillage		Shallow
tillage to prepare fine seedbed		Harrowing,
planking
Conservation
Tillage		Minimum
soil disturbance retaining crop residue on surface		Zero
tillage, minimum tillage
3. Classification of Essential Nutrients (
CO2)
Essential nutrients are
classified based on the quantity required by the plant.
CategoryNutrientsQuantity Required
Primary
(Macro)		Nitrogen,
Phosphorus, Potassium		Large
quantity
SecondaryCalcium,
Magnesium, Sulphur		Moderate
quantity
MicroZinc,
Iron, Boron, Manganese, Copper, Molybdenum, Chlorine		Trace
quantity
4. Soil Moisture Constants (
CO4)
Soil moisture constants describe
the different states of water held in the soil.
ConstantDescription
Gravitational
Water		Excess
water that drains freely under gravity; not available to plants for long
Capillary
Water		Water
held by capillary forces in soil pores; the main source of water available to
plants
Hygroscopic
Water		Water
tightly held on soil particle surfaces; not available to plants
